title: Test and wording LOWs from the WCLI-140 delta review (none blocking)
description: Follow-ups from the Opus delta review APPROVE at 71bdc7c of ward-cli#267 (WCLI-140). LOW-A: checkout.ts identityBindable has no test pinning writesInto = the ward directory. Add a case with a writable .git and an empty ward directory that is not writable (0o555), expecting inert with no registerHint; add R_OK when writesInto is the ward directory, since bindCheckoutIdentity opens it with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY; widen the comment on the writable-directory check. The comment hedging on ACLs and EROFS is looser than access() actually behaves; tighten it. LOW-B (runbook step 8): (1) tone: say "To replace it, and only if that checkout should have the project secrets, run ward init from it, then ward profile approve", matching reporting.ts and the DEC-255 (a6) intent, not an imperative; (2) "its checkout reads as unregistered" stops being true once registered; (3) 0.1.1 is framed two ways in step 8; note it where step 5 pins the tag. LOW-C: the unwritable-git test in test/reporting.test.ts should use test.skipIf(process.getuid?.() === 0) so a root run shows as skipped, not passed. LOW-D (record only): the runbook dropped the clause "the replacement matches profile, project and checkout root"; nothing is lost.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each LOW above is corrected, with a test that goes red when the writesInto ward-directory check is removed
lore check and bun run check stay green

implementationNotes: Implemented on fix/WCLI-145-review-lows. LOW-A: identityBindable now requires R_OK as well when writesInto is the existing ward directory (the bind opens it O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY), and its comment is rewritten (access() honours ACLs and read-only mounts; what it cannot see is a race or a refusal only the open raises). Two new reporting tests: a ward directory at 0o555 (not writable) and at 0o300 (not readable), each with a writable .git, expecting inert with no registerHint. Controls run: dropping the writesInto = directory assignment turns both red; dropping R_OK turns only the 0o300 case red. LOW-B: runbook step 8 now reads "To replace it, and only if that checkout should have the project secrets, run ward init from it, then ward profile approve"; "its checkout reads as unregistered" now says "until registered"; the 0.1.1 double framing is resolved inside step 8 by making the release history consistently past tense ("0.1.1 raised it from 2 to 3"), NOT by a note at step 5, because the documentation lore profile sits at its token budget and the step 5 note put it ~23 tokens over (max_tokens not raised). LOW-C: the unwritable-git test and the two new ones use test.skipIf(root). LOW-D recorded only: the runbook dropped the clause "the replacement matches profile, project and checkout root"; nothing is lost. bun run check 1224 pass; lore check, lore validate --strict and check-lore-agent-sources green.

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES

opum-ai/ward-cli#274 (WCLI-145) at 2bf1415726a2f6045fa9d123b09ab3136aa58c69. Reviewed from a tree read only, model claude-opus-5-5. The code and tests are clean. One runbook item fails acceptance criterion 0.

FINDINGS

1. BLOCKING (AC 0 "Each LOW above is corrected"; this is a docs wording defect): LOW-B(3), the double framing of 0.1.1, is still there. Files: docs/runbooks/install-and-upgrade-ward-from-a-release.md:57, :93, :97.
   - Step 5 (:57) pins the build being installed: `ward --version` prints `0.1.1`.
   - :93 still says "0.1.1 has no command to remove it; … a later release is expected to add one". That treats 0.1.1 as the build the reader is running.
   - :97 says "A 0.1.1 record and its binding have no checkout identity: until registered, its checkout reads as unregistered … run `ward init` … If init cannot give it an identity, it stays inert, with no hint". That treats 0.1.1 as an earlier build whose records are legacy.
   - The behaviour :97 describes (nonce, legacy records reading as unregistered, registerHint) is not in 0.1.1. ADR 0026:77 says "Existing 0.1.1 vaults still open, and their records never match", and ADR 0026:92 says "a 0.1.1 binary refuses it as malformed". package.json is still 0.1.1, so this is unreleased behaviour.
   - So a reader who installs v0.1.1 by step 5 gets a step 8 whose last paragraph does not apply to their binary.
   - The diff changed only :79 ("raises" to "raised"). That fixes one tense at one site; the two framings at :93 and :97 survive.
   - Your ruling lets the fix sit anywhere. On substance, though, step 8 is still not consistent with step 5's pinned tag.
   - Fixes that need no token-budget increase:
     - Reword :93 so it does not name 0.1.1 as the running build (for example "Ward has no command to remove it").
     - Mark the :97 paragraph as applying from the release after 0.1.1.
   - The wording is the writer's call.

2. No finding, Q1: the identityBindable change (src/adapters/checkout.ts:254-274) is correct and minimal.
   - R_OK is added only on the branch where an existing `ward` directory becomes writesInto. That matches the bind's O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY open at :171-178. When the bind mkdirs the directory itself (:164, mode 0o700), it opens a directory it just created, so the absent-directory branch correctly does not ask for R_OK.
   - Search (X) permission is covered on both paths:
     - X_OK is in `needs` from the start.
     - When the ward directory exists, `lstatSync(file)` at :261 needs X on it, and an EACCES there is not ENOENT, so it returns false before accessSync.
     - access() path resolution also requires search on every ancestor.
   - No gap is in scope.
   - The behaviour change is confined. `registrable` has one consumer, reporting.ts:488, and the only effect is inert with no registerHint where init would throw.
   - The accept half of the gate is proven: the existing test "is inert, with a hint, when its checkout has an empty ward directory" (test/reporting.test.ts, the empty-ward-directory case) still expects registerHint: true with a default-mode ward directory. So R_OK does not over-refuse.

3. No finding, Q2: the comment (checkout.ts:234-248) is true.
   - access(2) honours ACLs on macOS and Linux.
   - It reports EROFS for W_OK on a read-only mount.
   - "a refusal only the open itself raises (a security module, say)" is a fair example. AppArmor, the macOS sandbox and TCC refuse at open or mkdir. Linux SELinux is partly visible to access() through inode_permission, and the word "say" keeps the claim loose enough.
   - access() checks the real uid, not the effective one. "This account" is accurate because Ward is not setuid. A note at most, not a finding.

4. No finding, Q3: the tests are sound.
   - Dropping `writesInto = directory` makes access() check the 0o755 .git with W|X|R, which passes, so registerHint appears and both the 0o555 and 0o300 cases go red.
   - Dropping R_OK leaves 0o555 inert because W fails, so only 0o300 goes red. That matches the claim.
   - readCheckoutId returns undefined (ENOENT) in both fixtures. The cases reach identityBindable rather than going inert for an unrelated reason.
   - test.skipIf(asRoot) is correct: as root, access() grants R/W regardless of mode, so these cases would fail rather than pass. getuid being undefined off-POSIX gives false.
   - Fixture safety:
     - chmodSync(ward, mode) sits outside the try, and the restore to 0o755 is in finally.
     - A throw before the chmod leaves a 0o755 directory.
     - The directories are empty, so cleanup cannot fail.
     - The .git 0o555 test keeps its existing finally restore.

5. No finding, Q4: LOW-B(1) and (2) are corrected.
   - :99-100 reads "To replace it, and only if that checkout should have the project's secrets, run `ward init` from it, then `ward profile approve`". That is conditional and matches reporting.ts:496/:522 and the intent of DEC-255 (a6).
   - :97 "until registered" fixes the "reads as unregistered" overclaim.
   - Every other change in the runbook is a reflow of :93-95 ("it stays, authorising nothing"), with no change in meaning.
   - LOW-D was recorded only, as the task asks.

6. No finding, Q5: the PR touches no DEC-182 (1) fence-class path. The four files are the tracker record, the runbook, the named checkout identity check, and the test.

OUT OF DIFF, NOT BLOCKING (record only)
- runbook :93-94 "a later release is expected to add one [removal command]" is in tension with ADR 0026:86 "No cleanup command is filed". This predates the PR.
- reporting.ts:490's inert remedy, "its git directory or identity file is unusable", now also covers an unwritable, unsearchable or unreadable `ward` directory, which it does not name. This was already true for 0o555 before this PR.

- Whether released v0.1.1 actually shipped snapshot version 3, which is what ":79 0.1.1 raised it from 2 to 3" claims. ADR 0024 names the bump but not the release, and I could not read tags.
